patch_description: A fundamentally different architecture: instead of a single post-convolution noise gate, this design applies noise-scaled median snapping twice — once before and once after the exponential window convolution. The pre-convolution snap removes noise-sized steps from the raw signal so the windowed average operates on already-debiased data, compounding the smoothing effect on the output. The mechanism remains entirely in the level domain (no slope gating), which prior generations showed is strictly superior. By quantizing noise-sized deviations to the local median before averaging, the exponential convolution receives a cleaner input, reducing spurious slope changes at the output without adding lag, since median snapping is zero-phase and O(1) per sample with a small 5-tap window. This targets smoothness improvement while lag and tracking remain governed by the same window length, preserving responsiveness.
